cuts.reason: Cuts from the establishing two-shot down to a bird's-eye view of the restaurant right as the wife starts explaining the 'where to sit' saga, opening the visual gag about their indecision.
Jumps from the overhead layout shot into a tight front shot on the wife exactly as she lands the word 'restaurant,' snapping focus back to her face for the punchline of the setup sentence.
Cuts to an over-the-shoulder shot of her pointing and arguing with him, launching the physical bickering montage that visually illustrates 'discussing where to sit.'
Cuts to a wide shot of the couple walking past several tables, compressing their six minutes of indecision into a fast visual montage.
Quick cut into a tight close-up of the wife's scowling face, punctuating the montage rhythm with her exasperation over the table choice.
Reverse cut to a tight close-up of the husband pointing and scowling, completing the rapid back-and-forth rhythm of the argument montage.
Cuts wide to reveal the couple finally seated at a table, resolving the montage and giving the joke a beat of stillness before the punchline lines land.
Cuts in to a tight close-up on the wife's deadpan face right as she delivers 'No,' isolating the punchline setup for maximum reaction emphasis.
Cuts to a close-up of the husband's deadpan reaction immediately after 'Let's sit there,' landing on his silent, defeated expression as the sketch's button/punchline.
Cuts from the husband's reaction face to the black title/credit card, closing out the sketch with the show's branding.

reaction_shots.description: Tight close-up on the wife's scowling, unimpressed face during the table-selection montage.
Tight close-up on the husband's annoyed, pointing face mid-argument during the table-selection montage.
Extended close-up on the wife's flat, deadpan expression as she says 'No' and then 'Let's sit there,' the emotional core of the punchline.
Final close-up on the husband's silent, weary deadpan reaction as the title card fades in over his face -- the sketch's closing button.

pacing_notes: Opens with a leisurely ~3.4s establishing two-shot for the setup line, then explodes into a rapid-fire montage of five shots averaging under a second each (0.5-0.9s) as the dialogue describes the couple's six-minute table debate, mimicking their back-and-forth indecision through cutting rhythm alone. The pace then decelerates sharply: a ~2.2s held wide shot of them finally sitting, a ~2.5s close-up reaction shot for the 'No...Let's sit there' punchline, a brief ~0.9s final reaction shot as the button, and a longer ~1.4s outro title card to close. The whip-fast montage in the middle contrasted with the slow bookending shots is what sells both the joke's content and its punchline.
